page: OVHcloud b3-64 is a general-purpose virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided by a local 400 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is equipped with a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark evaluations, the b3-64 demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance via stress-ng and strong multi-threaded bzip3 decompression capabilities. Memory performance is a notable highlight, with passmark memory scores and large-block uncached read/write memory bandwidth tests placing in the top 25% of evaluated servers. Conversely, multi-core CPU performance, database operations, and Redis SET operations register in the average tier. Large-model LLM inference data is unavailable, but the server achieves strong text generation speeds with smaller 135M parameter models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated core allocation and NVMe storage provide a reliable resource density without the performance degradation risks of shared-core environments. The balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes this instance well-suited for general-purpose workloads, including web serving, medium-scale database operations, and multi-threaded data decompression tasks.
